guardian.title: Archaeologists uncover ancient Byzantine city in Egypt’s western desert
guardian.description:
Well-preserved fourth-century quarters reveal details of daily life, urban development and economic activities

Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a well-preserved Byzantine-era city in the western desert.

The fourth-century quarters had residential and religious structures, including a basilica-style church in the Dakhla oasis. Archaeologists also found coins, pottery fragments and tools.

guardian.description:

As Narendra Modi touched down in Seychelles over the weekend, the archipelago nation in the Indian Ocean swiftly bestowed one of its “highest” honours upon the Indian prime minister.

Modi beamed as he accepted the Guardian of the Blue Horizon award from Patrick Herminie, the Seychelles president, complete with a trophy and certificate.

guardian.description:
Authorities say rainy season getting deadlier, with Ghana reporting 13 dead and floods hitting Benin, Togo and Nigeria

Floods in Côte d’Ivoire have killed 59 people since May, the communication minister told a cabinet meeting in Abidjan.

There are fears the toll could further rise as rescue teams continue to search for victims during the rainy season, which runs from May until July, the minister, Amadou Coulibaly, added.

guardian.title: Cuban zoo celebrates birth of Bengal tigers amid energy crisis
guardian.description:
Arrival of endangered cats, including rare white cub, revitalises team straining under fuel and medicine shortages

For the Cuban zookeeper Ángel Cordero, the sight of four Bengal ⁠tiger cubs playing in a cage at the Cuban national zoo is a small miracle on an island stifled by shortages ⁠of fuel, medicine and ⁠days-long power outages.

The ​birth of these endangered big cats – including an exceedingly rare white tiger – has revitalised a team of zoo workers, he said.

guardian.description:
Interim president says unrest will not break out despite anger at official response to the 24 June disaster

Venezuela’s interim president has defended her country’s emergency response to the twin earthquakes that have killed more than 3,000 people, vowing the country would not descend into social unrest.

Many Venezuelans have expressed anger at what they see as the US-backed government’s inadequate response to the 24 June disaster before international teams arrived.

rfi.title: Merino's late strike takes Spain past Portugal into World Cup quarter-finals
rfi.description: Mikel Merino scored in second half stoppage time at the Dallas Stadium on Monday to send Spain past Portugal into the last eight at the 2026 World Cup and end the World Cup career of Portugal skipper Cristiano Ronaldo.

rfi.title: Rebels seize key-town of Anéfis as rebels tighten grip on northern Mali
rfi.description: Tuareg separatists and al-Qaeda affiliates appear to have secured control of a key town in northern Mali following a coordinated offensive by the rebels over the weekend. The Malian army and Russian mercenaries have been holed up in the key camp of Anéfis after the rebels launched their offensive on Saturday 4 July.

rfi.title: From memes to political movement, India's 'Cockroach' party leads youth revolt
rfi.description: India's Cockroach Janata Party began life as a series of internet memes and has grown into a real-life movement, bringing together young people angry about unemployment and alleged exam fraud. What began five weeks ago as a satirical response to comments by India's chief justice has become a fast-growing campaign which now has political ambitions, even as observers question whether it can survive without more effective organisation.

rfi.title: Hunger in northern Nigeria reaches worst levels in nearly a decade, WFP says
rfi.description: More than 17 million people across nine conflict-hit states in northern Nigeria face severe hunger, the UN's food agency (WFP) has said, warning that violence and funding ‌cuts are driving food insecurity to its worst level in nearly a decade. Stripped of their livelihoods, some people are fleeing across the border into neighbouring Benin.

lemonde.description: Les habitants d’Ille-sur-Têt, commune qui a été évacuée, sont sous le choc, alors que l’incendie de Trévillach, le plus important depuis cinquante ans dans la région, n’était pas encore fixé lundi soir. france24fr.title: Gaza : la dissolution des instances dirigeantes du Hamas, "un geste pour débloquer le plan Trump"
france24fr.description: Près de vingt ans après avoir pris le pouvoir dans la bande de Gaza, le Hamas a annoncé lundi lâcher les rênes du territoire au profit d'un comité de technocrates palestiniens. Jean-Paul Chagnollaud, professeur émérite et président d'honneur de l'Institut de recherche et d'études Méditerranée Moyen-Orient (iReMMO), décrypte les enjeux de cette décision.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026: "Kylian Mbappé nous rend fiers d'être Français"
france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce mardi 7 juillet, la nouvelle démonstration des capacités militaires de la Chine, qui a procédé, hier, à un tir d'essai de missile dans le Pacifique. Les réactions à l’annonce du Hamas de dissoudre son administration à Gaza. L’inquiétude face à la propagation rapide des incendies en Europe. L’élimination du Portugal par l’Espagne, 1 à 0, en 8èmes de finale du Mondial. Et le but de Kylian Mbappé contre une sénatrice paraguayenne raciste.

france24fr.title: En direct : fin du suspense pour Marine Le Pen, bientôt fixée sur son avenir présidentiel
france24fr.description: C'est le jour J pour Marine Le Pen, qui va savoir si elle pourra être candidate à l'élection présidentielle de 2027. La cour d'appel du tribunal de Paris doit rendre mardi son jugement dans l'affaire des assistants parlementaires des eurodéputés du Front national. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Trump, la Fifa et le carton rouge de Balogun : qu’en pensent les Américains ?
france24fr.description: Un président peut-il influencer une décision de la Fifa ? C’est ce que revendique Donald Trump, qui affirme être intervenu directement auprès de l'instance du football pour obtenir l'annulation du carton rouge de l’attaquant américain Folarin Balogun. Alors que la polémique enfle, à Boston, ville hôte de la Coupe du monde, nous avons demandé aux Américains ce qu'ils en pensaient.

france24fr.title: Ukraine en direct : plus de 430 drones ukrainiens lancés vers Moscou, avant le sommet de l'Otan
france24fr.description: L'Ukraine a lancé plus de 430 drones vers Moscou dans la nuit, a annoncé mardi le maire de la capitale. Une personne a par ailleurs été tuée dans la région russe de Belgorod, rapporte le gouverneur régional. Ces attaques interviennent alors que s'ouvre le sommet de l'Otan à Ankara, pour relancer les efforts diplomatiques pour mettre fin à la guerre en Ukraine. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Un Français va arbitrer l'Argentine contre l'Égypte et ses supporters crient au scandale
france24fr.description: La nomination de l'arbitre français François Letexier pour le huitième de finale entre l'Argentine et l'Égypte, mardi, inquiète les fans argentins. Sur fond de rivalité entre les deux finalistes du Mondial 2022, ils craignent la partialité de celui qui est surtout connu dans le pays pour avoir déclenché "l'affaire Prestianni".

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : résultats, articles et temps forts de la nuit
france24fr.description: L'ingérence de Trump auprès de la Fifa, l'Espagne qui élimine le Portugal et la Belgique qui corrige les États-Unis... Retrouvez les résultats des matches disputés dans la nuit, les temps forts et les derniers articles de France 24 sur la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Donald Trump n'a pas suffi : les États-Unis humiliés par la Belgique et éliminés de leur Mondial
Donald Trump n'a pas suffi : les États-Unis humiliés par la Belgique et éliminés de leur Mondial
france24fr.description: Fin de parcours pour les États-Unis. Le Team USA a été éliminé par la Belgique en huitièmes de finale, lundi à Seattle (4-1). Les Américains n'ont pas pesé sur la rencontre, malgré la présence de Balogun, dont la suspension a été annulée par la Fifa après une demande de Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: États-Unis - Belgique : les Diables Rouges n'ont laissé aucune chance au Team USA
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis affrontaent la Belgique lundi à Seattle en 8es de finale du Mondial 2026. Un match sous tension après la polémique provoquée par la levée de la suspension de l'Américain Balogun par la Fifa, pour laquelle Donald Trump est intervenu. Une rencontre à revivee avec le live commenté de nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: La Knesset adopte en première lecture la création d'une commission d'enquête sur le 7-Octobre
france24fr.description: Le Parlement israélien a approuvé lundi en première lecture une proposition de loi établissant une commission d'enquête bipartisane sur les défaillances sécuritaires ayant conduit à l'attaque du 7 octobre 2023, qui a entraîné la mort de plus de 1 200 personnes. Défendue par le Premier ministre Benjamin Netanyahu, cette proposition est rejetée par l'opposition qui a boycotté le vote.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Espagne élimine sur le fil le Portugal de Cristiano Ronaldo
Mondial 2026 : l'Espagne met à la retraite Cristiano Ronaldo et rejoint les quarts
france24fr.description: L'Espagne a remporté le derby ibérique lundi face au Portugal en huitièmes de finale de la Coupe du monde (1-0). La lumière est venue d'un but tardif du remplaçant Mikel Merino, après un coup franc qu'il a lui-même provoqué. Ça sent la fin pour le Portugais Cristiano Ronaldo, qui n'a pas pesé sur le match.

france24fr.title: La canicule donne des sueurs froides aux compagnies d'assurance
france24fr.description: L'été commence à peine que la France traverse déjà sa troisième vague de fortes chaleurs en moins de deux mois. La canicule s'accompagne de son chapelet de mauvaises nouvelles : annulations d'événements culturels et sportifs, de Solidays à Paris à l'IronMan de Nice mais aussi une pression encore plus forte que par le passé sur l'agriculture et l'élevage, deux activités très météo-dépendantes. En 2025, la canicule avait coûté 1,7 milliard d'euros au secteur de l'assurance, soit 15% de plus que la

france24fr.title: La France retire ses diplomates du Burkina Faso
france24fr.description: Le personnel diplomatique du Burkina Faso doit quitter la France d'ici ce lundi soir. Une mesure qui intervient une semaine après la décision unilatérale des autorités burkinabè de rompre les relations diplomatiques avec Paris. Paris qui annonce également le retour dans l'hexagone de tous ses diplomates en provenance du Burkina Faso.

france24fr.title: Emmanuel Macron en Syrie : pourquoi cette visite ?
france24fr.description: C'est une visite inédite pour un chef de l'état de l'Union européenne depuis la chute de Bachar El Assad, qu'a entamé lundi Emmanuel Macron. Le président français est en Syrie. Accompagné d'une délégation de chefs d'entreprise, il est venu assurer le dirigeant syrien Ahmed Al Charaa du soutien de la France en matière de reconstruction économique et faire le pari d'une transition politique réussie.

france24fr.title: Certaines images des funérailles d'Ali Khamenei dopées par l'Intelligence Artificielle
france24fr.description: Énormément d'images circulent sur les réseaux sociaux depuis le début des funérailles d'Ali Khamenei, l'ancien Guide Suprême iranien tué par des frappes américano-israéliennes. Si une foule très large a bien assisté à ces funérailles, beaucoup de publications essaient d'amplifier encore le phénomène. Décryptage dans Info Intox avec Jules Boiteau.

zeit.title: Unwetter: Tote und Vermisste nach Fluten und Erdrutsch in China
Abi 2026: Lehrerverband beklagt: Zu gute Abiturnoten schaffen Probleme
Kriminalität: Weitere Ermittlungen nach tödlichen Schüssen in Offenburg
Fußball-Weltmeisterschaft: Das war die WM-Nacht: USA mit Balogun raus, Spanien weiter
Gründungen in Deutschland: KI-Nutzung sorgt für Gründungsrekord bei deutschen Start-ups
zeit.description: In Deutschland werden so viele Start-ups gegründet wie noch nie: Im ersten Halbjahr entstanden 3.053 neue Firmen. Der Startup-Verband sieht KI als zentralen Treiber.

zeit.title: Wetteraussichten: Wolken halten sich hartnäckig in NRW - örtlich Regen
Reiseverkehr: Zum Ferienstart ist Geduld auf Autobahnen gefragt
Grüne Oase für Blinde: Duft als Wegweiser: Botanischer Blindengarten bleibt Rarität
Raketentest im Pazifik: USA reagieren mit »großer Besorgnis« auf chinesischen Raketentest
zeit.description: Die USA haben Chinas jüngsten Raketentest im Südpazifik kritisiert. China solle seine Verpflichtungen als ständiges Mitglied im UN-Sicherheitsrat einhalten.

zeit.title: Gründerbranche: Zahl der neuen Start-ups in Hessen steigt rasant
Krankenstand: Immer mehr Arbeitnehmer fallen wegen Krankheit länger aus
zeit.description: Wegen langer Ausfälle müssen die Krankenkassen mehr Geld für das Krankengeld aufwenden. Psychische Erkrankungen gehören zu den häufigsten Ursachen.

zeit.title: Nato-Gipfel in der Türkei: Der Gipfel der Widersprüche
zeit.description: Die Türkei richtet den Nato-Gipfel aus und zeigt sich innenpolitisch immer autoritärer. Was sagen die Bündnispartner dazu? Und: Urteil über Le Pens politische Zukunft

zeit.title: Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Von der Dicke der Pasta beim Spaghettieis und anderen wichtigen Fragen
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Dienstag – Mit einer Reform der Kita-Gebühren, schlechter Auftragslage im Hamburger Wohnungsbau und der Suche nach Ebola-Patient null

zeit.title: 100. Podcastjubiläum: Denk mal an übermorgen! Was macht das mit dir?
zeit.description: Der Krisenpodcast wird 100! Petra und Stefan feiern mit den besten Beams: Gedankenreisen in eine gelingende Zukunft. Und fragen sich und euch: Wie soll es weitergehen?

zeit.title: Spirituosensteuer: Spirituosenfirmen zweifeln an Mehreinnahmen durch höhere Alkoholsteuer
zeit.description: Die Koalition will die Steuern auf Spirituosen anheben. Der Bund rechnet mit fast einer halben Milliarde Euro an Mehreinnahmen im Jahr. Die Alkoholindustrie widerspricht.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Fussball-WM 2026: Nach dem Skandal um Balogun beendet Belgien die WM-Party der USA +++ Spanien bezwingt Portugal mit 1:0 und steht im Viertelfinal
nzz.description: Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten zur Fussball-WM in Kanada, Mexiko und den USA.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Crans-Montana: Die Region Lombardei tritt als Zivilklägerin auf
nzz.description: In der Bar «Le Constellation» im Skiort Crans-Montana im Wallis ist es in der Neujahrsnacht zu einem verheerenden Brand gekommen. 41 Personen sind ums Leben gekommen. Die Ermittlungen laufen. Wir geben einen Überblick über den Stand der Dinge.

nzz.title: Belgien zerlegt die USA 4:1 – Heimturnier ist zu Ende
nzz.description: Nachdem es viel Wirbel um eine zurückgenommene Rote Karte für Amerikas Topstürmer Folarin Balogun gab, blieben die Gastgeber gegen Belgien schwach.

nzz.title: Der Bund lässt Strafverfolgung gegen die Ex-Fedpol-Chefin Nicoletta della Valle zu. Sie sagt, die Schweiz könnte damit zu einem «Hort für Hassprediger» werden
nzz.description: Der NDB, das SEM und die Fedpol-Juristen sahen keinen Grund, gegen den antiisraelischen Journalisten Ali Abunimah ein Einreiseverbot zu verhängen. Doch dann intervenierte die ehemalige oberste Polizistin der Schweiz. Aus politischen Gründen, sagt Abunimah.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Eltern wollen keine Söhne mehr: Das Mädchen ist das neue Trophy-Kid
nzz.description: Viele Eltern wünschen sich heute Töchter und bezahlen sogar in Kinderwunschkliniken dafür. Was als Fortschritt und Emanzipation verkauft wird, ist das Gegenteil: Wachsende biologistische Stereotype schaden allen.

nzz.title: In Liechtenstein sollen Wärmepumpen künftig auch zur Kühlung eingesetzt werden
nzz.description: Klimaanlagen unterliegen im Fürstentum erheblichen Restriktionen. Doch mobile Anlagen sind ohne Bewilligung erlaubt.

nzz.title: Milliardär contra Fiskus: Der reichste Franzose findet, er werde schon genug vom Staat geschröpft
nzz.description: Bernard Arnault zieht wegen einer Steuernachzahlung vor Frankreichs höchstes Verwaltungsgericht. Der Chef des Luxusgüterkonzerns LVMH hat genug davon, dass der Staat immer tiefer in seine Taschen greift.

nzz.title: Wird Elon Musk bald SpaceX und Tesla fusionieren? Die Aktionäre werden sich ihm kaum in den Weg stellen
nzz.description: Die Spekulationen, dass der Raketenbauer SpaceX den Elektroauto-Pionier Tesla übernehmen wird, reissen einen Monat nach dem Börsengang von SpaceX nicht ab.

nzz.title: PODCAST «NZZ AKZENT» - Warum der Vatikan die radikalen Piusbrüder exkommuniziert
nzz.description: Vier neue Bischöfe hat die Piusbruderschaft im Wallis geweiht – gegen den klaren Willen von Papst Leo XIV. Dessen Antwort und dessen Strafe folgten prompt. Die Piusbrüder sind exkommuniziert. Weitermachen werden sie trotzdem.

nzz.title: Dürre in der Schweiz: Die Trockenheit verschärft sich weiter
nzz.description: Die Gewitter in der vergangenen Woche haben nur kurzfristig für Entspannung gesorgt. Zunehmend mangelt es Böden, Gewässern und Grundwasservorkommen an Wasser. Die Waldbrandgefahr steigt. Eine Momentaufnahme.

nzz.title: Schicksalstag für Marine Le Pen: Kann die Ikone der französischen Rechten doch noch zur Wahl 2027 antreten?
nzz.description: Am Dienstag entscheidet ein Gericht darüber, ob Marine Le Pen 2027 für das Präsidentenamt kandidieren kann. Sollte die langjährige Chefin des Rassemblement national unterliegen, steht Jordan Bardella als Ersatzkandidat bereit.

nzz.title: Bereit für Historisches: Die Energiekurve der Schweiz zeigt vor dem WM-Achtelfinal gegen Kolumbien steil nach oben
nzz.description: Vor drei Wochen war die Stimmung im Fussball-Nationalteam angespannt. Doch die Kritikkultur erweist sich als grosse Stärke dieser Mannschaft. Nun ist der Achtelfinal nicht gut genug.

nzz.title: Eine zerrüttete Nation, ein gemeinsamer Fussballtraum: Kolumbien hofft auf den grossen Titel
nzz.description: Das von Konflikten und Drogengewalt gebeutelte Land ist verrückt nach Fussball. Nun soll der Bayern-Star Luis Díaz an der WM auch gegen die Schweiz brillieren.

nzz.title: Gezerre ums Budget: Die EU braucht mehr Geld, das die Mitgliedsländer selber gerne hätten
nzz.description: In der EU wird über das nächste Budget, 2028 bis 2034, verhandelt. Die Debatten zeigen, in welcher schlechten finanziellen Lage Europa ist. Die Schuldenspirale dreht sich immer schneller.

nzz.title: Lange Haftstrafe: Hochrangiger syrischer Geheimdienstgeneral in Wien wegen Folter verurteilt
nzz.description: In Österreich wurde der bisher höchstrangige Vertreter des gestürzten Asad-Regimes juristisch zur Verantwortung gezogen. Laut dem Gericht liess er in einem von ihm geleiteten Gefängnis in Rakka Oppositionelle systematisch foltern.

nzz.title: Peking verteilt Milliarden an die Industrie. China leidet selbst darunter
nzz.description: Europa klagt schon lange über chinesische Subventionen, die Unternehmen gelten als extrem wettbewerbsfähig. Die Kehrseite des Staatskapitalismus ist jedoch Ineffizienz.

observador.title: A chegada dos ingleses (independência americana 1)
observador.description: Há 250 anos, a 4 de Julho de 1776, os EUA tornaram-se independentes. Os colonos britânicos tinham-se instalado lá no séc. XVII. Este é o primeiro de quatro programas sobre a independência americana

observador.title: Desidratação: os sinais que nunca associou a falta de água
observador.description: Quando pensamos em desidratação, pensamos logo em sede. Mas esse pode ser um dos últimos sinais. Antes disso, o organismo pode dar pistas inesperadas que muitos de nós ignoramos.

observador.title: O que explica este caos nos exames nacionais?
observador.description: A classificação digital dos exames está a acumular falhas e já obrigou ao adiamento de prazos. Mariana Marques Tiago explica o que correu mal e o que isto significa para alunos e professores.

observador.title: 4h. Arranca hoje a cimeira da NATO na Turquia
observador.description: Com foco no reforço do investimento em Defesa bem como no apoio à Ucrânia. No Campeonato do Mundo, a Bélgica venceu os Estados Unidos por 4-1.

observador.title: Os "Diabos" cancelaram os planos da FIFA e de Trump
observador.description: A Bélgica venceu os Estados Unidos (com Balogun) por 4-1 e defronta a Espanha na próxima fase do Mundial. Rudi Garcia não tem medo de sentar "Vacas sagradas" e consegue vencer com caras novas.

observador.title: 3h. Durão Barroso apela a sentimento de comunidade nacional
observador.description: E diz que Portugal  não pode descurar a vocação atlântica nem o sentimento de pertença à Europa. Ainda, a Bélgica venceu os Estados Unidos por 4-1.

observador.title: Para já, a notícia é esta: a equipa da casa foi goleada
observador.description: Admitindo que não há nenhuma regra para anular frangos nem validar defesas de Courtois a remates de Balogun, EUA caíram perante uma Bélgica que, como diz Klopp, sabe a quem pertence o futebol (1-4).

observador.title: Mourinho deixou de ser opção, Jesus tornou-se a única via
observador.description: Mourinho ainda foi hipótese caso Martínez saísse depois da Liga das Nações, Jesus passou da short list para candidato único à sucessão do espanhol nos últimos meses. Próximos dias vão fechar processo.

observador.title: 2h. Ronaldo confirma que este foi o último mundial
observador.description: Sobre a permanência na Seleção Nacional Ronaldo diz que ainda tem tempo para decidir. Ainda, o Governo prolongou a situação de alerta de incêndio até quinta-feira.

observador.title: O que mostrou o rosto de Ronaldo na "última dança"
observador.description: Chegou ao estádio a brincar com as câmaras, entrou no relvado a sorrir, deixou o campo a conter as lágrimas e abandonou o estádio "triste". O Observador analisa à lupa a despedida de Ronaldo.

observador.title: 1h. Roberto Martínez confirma que vai abandonar a Seleção
observador.description: Sobre a eliminação da equipa das quinas diz que os detalhes fizeram a diferença no jogo. Ainda, Ventura quer um debate urgente sobre os problemas e atrasos que se têm registado nos exames nacionais.

observador.title: "É o fim do jogador cuja longevidade tem sido uma maravilha"
observador.description: Na imprensa internacional ecoa a saída de Martínez e o fim de Ronaldo em Mundiais. Lágrimas do capitão, exemplo de longevidade e prestação aquém na América do Norte no epicentro do rescaldo.

observador.title: Não deu Portugal e festa foi feita pelos nuestros hermanos
observador.description: Portugal está fora do Mundial de Futebol. Perdeu contra a vizinha Espanha com um golo marcado já nos descontos. Roberto Martínez deixa de ser selecionador e o futuro de Ronaldo é ainda incerto.

observador.title: Buckingham retira convite a Harry para estadia no palácio
observador.description: Harry aterrou no Reino Unido mas ficou sem alojamento no Palácio de Buckingham. As duas partes deram versões contraditórias, com questões de segurança e um processo judicial no centro da discórdia.

observador.title: Mais cinco defesas de Diogo a vingar aquela saída em 2022
observador.description: Diogo Costa voltou a ser o grande destaque de Portugal frente à Espanha e terminou Mundial-2026 como principal figura depois do lance infeliz no Mundial-2022 frente a Marrocos que demorou a esquecer.

observador.title: Cometa 3I/ATLAS pode ser muito mais velho do que o Sol
observador.description: O VLT do ESO mediu pela primeira vez a composição química de um cometa extrassolar. As conclusões, publicadas na Nature Astronomy, apontam para uma estrela anfitriã muito antiga.

observador.title: 30 terminais Multibanco para freguesias sem banco
observador.description: O "Multibanco + Perto" usa SmartPOS para levar 90% das operações de caixa automático a cerca de 740 mil pessoas no interior sem acesso a serviços bancários.

observador.title: SINTAP exige pagamento de subsídio de férias nas IPSS
observador.description: Sindicato reconhece dificuldades das IPSS nos Açores, mas deixa apelo ao Governo Regional para desenvolver "todas as diligências necessárias junto do Governo da República".

spiegel.title: Moskau: Bürgermeister meldet ukrainischen Drohnenangriff
spiegel.description: Vor Beginn des Nato-Gipfels intensivieren sich die Angriffe zwischen Moskau und Kyjiw. Mehr als 400 ukrainische Drohnen seien auf die russische Hauptstadt zugeflogen. Laut dem Bürgermeister wurden die meisten abgefangen.

spiegel.title: TKMS-U-Boote für Kanada: So fädelte die Bundes-Regierung den Megadeal ein
spiegel.description: Kanada will bei der deutschen TKMS-Werft bis zu zwölf U-Boote bestellen. Um das 20-Milliarden-Geschäft an Land zu ziehen, startete die Bundesregierung eine Charmeoffensive – und legte einen besonderen Köder aus.

spiegel.title: Charlotte Engelhardt spricht über ihre größte »Red Flag« bei Männern
spiegel.description: Was weist darauf hin, dass eine Beziehung schieflaufen könnte? Moderatorin Charlotte Engelhardt hat erklärt, welches Verhalten bei ihr die Alarmglocken schrillen lässt.

spiegel.title: Krankschreibungen: Krankenkassen sehen lange Ausfälle als größten Kostentreiber
spiegel.description: Mit der Krankschreibung ab dem ersten Tag möchte die Regierung Fehlzeiten eindämmen. Eine Analyse von Krankenkassen kommt nun zu dem Schluss: Langwierige Erkrankungen sind die Kostentreiber.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM News heute: Folarin Balogun versteht Aufregung wegen seiner Roten Karte – »natürlich kontrovers«
spiegel.description: Der US-Spieler im Zentrum des Skandals um die Rote Karte und Donald Trump hat sich erstmals selbst geäußert. Und Frankreich kündigt rechtliche Schritte nach dem Rassismus-Eklat gegen Kylian Mbappé an. Alles Wichtige zur WM.

spiegel.title: Straße von Hormus: Crew meldet Angriff auf Tanker
spiegel.description: Mit dem Abkommen zwischen den USA und Iran sollte sich der Schiffsverkehr in der Straße von Hormus eigentlich wieder normalisieren. Nun wurde offenbar erneut ein Tanker vor der Küste Omans beschossen. Woher, ist noch unklar.

spiegel.title: Nato-Gipfel in Ankara: Hauptsache, Trump ist happy
spiegel.description: Nur widerwillig reist US-Präsident Trump zum Nato-Gipfel in Ankara an. Es könnte ein Schicksalstreffen für die transatlantische Allianz werden. Diese fünf Player stehen im Mittelpunkt.

spiegel.title: Franziska Giffey präsentiert ihre liebsten Rezepte aus Berlin. Wer soll das essen?
News: Marine Le Pen, Frankreich, Nato-Gipfel, Folarin Balogun, Donald Trump
spiegel.description: Richter entscheiden über die Präsidentschaftskandidatur einer Rechtspopulistin. Der Nato-Gipfel beginnt – ein Grund für Putin, noch mehr Bomben zu schicken. Und: alle Augen auf Folarin Balogun. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Trump gibt Startschuss für Neugeborenen-Konten
spiegel.description: Unter dem Namen »Trump Accounts« sollen Babys in den USA ein Wertpapierkonto mit je 1000 Dollar bekommen. Donald Trump feiert die Initiative. Seine Landsleute kämpfen allerdings mit ganz anderen Problemen.

spiegel.title: Fahrradtour planen: So gelingt die perfekte Reise – Tipps von Profi Jana Kesenheimer
spiegel.description: Sie gewinnt Ultra-Rennen und hat Europa mehrfach auf zwei Rädern durchquert. Hier sagt Jana Kesenheimer, worauf es bei langen Touren per Fahrrad ankommt – und warum sie keine Wechselsocken braucht.

spiegel.title: Gleichgewicht: Gelingen Ihnen diese 30-Sekunden-Übungen?
spiegel.description: Ein gutes Balancegefühl erleichtert den Alltag – und es kann die Lebenserwartung erhöhen. Testen Sie sich, und sehen Sie in fünf Videos, wie Sie Ihr Gleichgewicht trainieren.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 live: USA - Belgien im Liveticker - Belgien kickt Gastgeber aus dem Turnier
spiegel.description: US-Keeper Freese leistet sich einen irren Patzer und steht damit sinnbildlich für sein Team. Balogun ist kein entscheidender Faktor. Und bei Belgien müssen es nicht immer die Altstars richten. Der Livekommentar im Minutenprotokoll.

spiegel.title: Walmart senkt Lebensmittelpreise – angeblich auf Bitten von Trump
spiegel.description: Der lange Arm des US-Präsidenten reicht offenbar bis zur Fleischtheke im Supermarkt. Auf seine Aufforderung hin habe Walmart die Preise gesenkt, verkündet Donald Trump. Hackfleisch koste fast 15 Prozent weniger. Walmart nennt eine andere Zahl.

spiegel.title: WM-Skandal um Gianni Infantino und Donald Trump: Fifa äußert sich zu Folarin-Balogun-Entscheidung

new-sci.title: Audacious mission to rescue NASA's falling telescope has launched
new-sci.description: NASA’s Swift space telescope is reaching the end of its two-decade run in orbit – unless a satellite launched on 3 July can give it a lifesaving boost

new-sci.title: Orangutan mothers seem to plan playdates for their offspring
new-sci.description: Female orangutans are generally solitary, but they travel more and eat less in an apparent effort to ensure their offspring have someone to play with

new-sci.title: This thoughtful book will make you look at the wonders of trees anew
new-sci.description: Aya Koda's Tree is an account of the late writer's visits to Japan's most famous, and ancient, trees. Featured in Wim Wenders's film Perfect Days, it is original and thought-provoking, says Rowan Hooper

new-sci.title: Stunning photos reveal the intricate beauty of fungi
new-sci.description: The vibrant colours and delicate details of New Zealand's fungi and slime moulds are documented in these images, taken from Jay Lichter's new book The Secret Life of Fungi

new-sci.title: Evocative photos of Canadian Arctic win New Scientist Editors Award
new-sci.description: Natalya Saprunova's photo series exploring coastal erosion and permafrost thaw across Inuvialuit territories in Canada has won the New Scientist Editors Award at the Earth Photo 2026 competition

new-sci.title: June heatwave may have killed around 20,000 people in Europe
new-sci.description: It will be some months before the true toll of Europe's worst-ever heatwave is confirmed, but researchers can estimate a death count based on how many people died in Europe during previous hot periods

phys-org.title: New biobased polymers exhibit excellent tensile properties beyond polyolefins
phys-org.description: The research group of Professor Kotohiro Nomura, Tokyo Metropolitan University, in cooperation with the research groups of Senior Researcher Hiroshi Hirano and Director Seiji Higashi of the Osaka Research Institute of Industrial Science and Technology, and Associate Professor Hiroki Takeshita of The University of Shiga Prefecture, has developed biobased poly(ester amide)s from inedible biorenewables that can be easily chemically recycled and exhibit better mechanical (tensile) properties in film

phys-org.title: Newly discovered mineral named for researcher Tyler Spano
phys-org.description: Tyler Spano's impact on the field of mineralogy is anything but small. So when a newly discovered mineral, modest in size but significant in meaning, was named spanoite in her honor, it became a fitting tribute to her contributions to the field.

phys-org.title: Q&A: Harnessing climate investments to serve development goals
phys-org.description: Climate pledges are designed to help countries reduce emissions and adapt to a changing climate, but the current iterations of these pledges place additional stresses on vulnerable nations, an international team of researchers co-led by University of Michigan Engineering and KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Sweden has shown.

phys-org.title: How an interstellar comet sheds light on universe's 'cosmic noon'
phys-org.description: Last year, an interstellar traveler entered our solar system. Some speculated that it was an alien spacecraft, but it turned out to be a comet, 3I/Atlas, and it provoked interest from astronomers and astrophysicists eager for insights into galaxies far, far away. Detailed observations from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) shot down the alien spacecraft idea, but recent NASA analysis holds clues about the comet's ancient and, literally, alien origins.

phys-org.title: Efficient method for preparing pseudopregnant mice promotes laboratory animal welfare
phys-org.description: In biomedical research using mouse models, preparing pseudopregnant recipient females is a standard step in embryo transfer protocols. Conventionally, this process requires technicians to select female mice showing clear signs of estrus. Because only a limited percentage of mice naturally enter this stage daily, facilities often maintain a relatively large stock of female mice. phys-org.title: What everyone gets wrong about the modern job search—and what actually works
phys-org.description: Job searching has never been more accessible—or more confusing. Platforms like LinkedIn, Indeed and employer career pages let candidates submit applications with just a few clicks. What happens after they click "submit," however, has become fertile ground for misinformation.

phys-org.title: AI system translates protein sequences into text, helping reveal functions of unknown proteins
phys-org.description: In a paper published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, researchers from Technion and Tel Aviv University present BetaDescribe, an AI system that translates protein sequences into natural-language descriptions, opening a new path toward understanding protein functions and accelerating drug development and material design.

phys-org.title: Newly identified marine bacterial enzyme opens new route to building bioactive compound libraries
phys-org.description: Many important medicines and agricultural compounds have origins in natural products made by microorganisms. One such compound is prodigiosin, a vivid red pigment produced by certain bacteria. Beyond its color, prodigiosin and related compounds known as prodiginines have attracted scientific interest because they have shown antibacterial, anticancer, immunosuppressive, antifungal and plant-protection activities.

phys-org.title: Soil thickness controls landslide occurrence, study finds
phys-org.description: Researchers at University of Tsukuba analyzed high-resolution topographic data from airborne LiDAR to examine the relationships among landslide area, depth, and slope gradient.

phys-org.title: Why customers stick with troubled brands: Emotional attachment may override perceived risk
phys-org.description: Strong emotional attachment to a brand may help explain why some consumers remain loyal even in the wake of negative publicity, according to research published in the International Journal of Business and Emerging Markets.

phys-org.title: Wasted pumpkin peel can keep your food fresh
phys-org.description: Researchers at Kyushu University have developed a new food preservation solution. Using pumpkin peel as a raw material, they synthesized a nanomaterial for food packaging that slows the deterioration of fruit and other produce while reducing transport damage. The findings were published April 30, 2026, in Food Research International.

phys-org.title: Quantum computing: Laser-optical system offers full control over 2,000 trapped Rydberg atoms
phys-org.description: Fraunhofer ILT in Aachen has developed a highly complex laser-optical system for a quantum computer currently under construction at the 5th Institute of Physics at the University of Stuttgart. This system enables 2,000 Rydberg atoms to be positioned with submicrometer precision in the computer's highly compact vacuum chamber. phys-org.title: Cultural power distance limits classroom voices across three communication pathways, review finds
phys-org.description: A systematic review of research on intercultural communication in higher education finds that cultural "power distance," which is the extent to which people accept unequal authority, continues to shape who speaks, who is heard and how knowledge is shared in multicultural classrooms.

phys-org.title: How to create the blackest black ever known: From nature to nanotechnology
phys-org.description: Achieving the blackest of blacks has been one of humanity's enduring challenges. It is a frontier that unites modern nanotechnologists with nature's ancient color palette.

phys-org.title: Stored water can develop slimy bacterial films: Nanotechnology may be a solution
phys-org.description: When drinking water is stored in containers, a thin layer of microorganisms can grow at the interface of the container and water. This thin layer is called a biofilm. It's made up of bacteria that make the water unsafe to drink. Slimy biofilms are harder to kill with ordinary disinfectants like chlorine. So scientists are always looking for new ways to clean water in household storage systems.

phys-org.title: Raft of targeted conservation efforts may help boost leopard numbers in sub-Saharan Africa, study suggests
phys-org.description: There could be fewer leopards living across sub-Saharan Africa than previously believed, according to a new study that has analyzed suitable habitat and conditions. It is hoped that the research, led by conservation scientists at Nottingham Trent University, could be used to help plan vital recovery efforts and focus conservation where it is most needed.

phys-org.title: Hummingbirds speed up pineapple family's evolution
phys-org.description: Hummingbirds make bromeliad plants split into new species twice as fast as other pollinators do, scientists at the University of Reading have found. The research team gathered records of which animals pollinate 403 types of bromeliad, which include pineapples and more than 3,700 species, and found three in four of these plants are visited by hummingbirds.

phys-org.title: Heat waves: Expert tips on redesigning UK homes to cope with hotter temperatures
phys-org.description: As the UK prepares for the third heat wave of 2026, most people will be hoping to keep cool at home. Building regulations to protect homes from overheating were introduced in 2022. These require all new homes to be checked at the design stage to see if they might be at risk of overheating. If the overheating risk is high, the architect has to make changes to the design.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Acceptable Path for Designer Babies
proj-syn.description: Genetic-engineering tools with which to design one's progeny already exist, and they are being made even more potent with AI—at least for those who can afford such services. In the absence of policy interventions, we will be hurtling toward a tiered society in which economic privileges become biological advantages.

proj-syn.title: The Democratic Turkey NATO Needs
proj-syn.description: At NATO's upcoming summit in Ankara, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will seek to portray his country as stable, confident, and essential to Western security. But only the last one is true, which is why the restoration of democracy in Turkey is more than a domestic concern.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup as It Should Be
proj-syn.description: While Donald Trump was widely expected to lord over this year’s World Cup, which the United States is co-hosting with Mexico and Canada, it has turned out not to be his scene. National teams populated with immigrants, and small-town America’s embrace of the event, go against everything Trump’s MAGA movement stands for.

proj-syn.title: The Real Threat to NATO
proj-syn.description: The greatest challenge to NATO comes not from its adversaries but from within. As its leaders gather in Ankara on July 7-8, they should focus less on military capabilities than on reinvigorating the alliance's founding strategic philosophy, centered on democratic legitimacy, human rights, and the rule of law.

proj-syn.title: How the EU Can Lead the Rest of the West
proj-syn.description: While Europe is not just another middle power, nor is it a great power with sufficient economic, military, and geopolitical clout to dictate terms on the global stage. Instead, Europe is the ideal candidate to convene and lead a group of like-minded middle powers, not as a US-style hegemon, but as a first among equals.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Face the World on Its Own
proj-syn.description: Under pressure from Russian aggression—which has reached its full expression in the ongoing war against Ukraine—and an increasingly hostile US administration, Europe urgently needs to make progress toward a defense union. But that will require Franco-German leadership of the kind that is not yet on offer.

proj-syn.title: How Safe Are Today’s Blockbuster Tech Stocks?
proj-syn.description: Today’s wave of mega-IPOs has unleashed a wave of analogies to past booms. While no analogy is perfect, an especially apposite—and sobering—case may be what followed Nippon Telegraph and Telephone’s IPO in February 1987.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dolce Vita?
proj-syn.description: Glacial growth, aging welfare states, and a shortage of centrist leaders suggest Europe faces a major debt crisis in the years ahead. But its emphasis on leisure over work could become a decisive advantage, positioning the continent as the leading model for thriving in an age of AI-driven abundance.

proj-syn.title: The Putin Escalation Risk
proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. The temptation to escape his predicament through a game-changing attack will grow stronger.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s New German Question
proj-syn.description: Without a EU-level framework capable of turning resources into scale, the bloc’s defense capabilities will remain limited, no matter how much member countries spends. If Germany, in particular, insists on going it alone, Europe could remain fully dependent on the US for key assets.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
proj-syn.description: While Nobel laureate economists Paul Krugman and Philippe Aghion disagree over how to measure Europe’s productivity gap with the United States, both overlook the value of its accumulated assets. That blind spot obscures the real story: Europe is living off a remarkable inheritance it has yet to convert into new growth.

proj-syn.title: NATO Needs a Defense Market
proj-syn.description: To convert NATO members' resources into military capabilities, setting defense as a strategic priority, increasing spending, and improving procurement systems are all steps in the right direction. But member countries will need to expand their industrial capacity—and that requires much more.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Choices Shaping our Children’s Health
proj-syn.description: Around the world, childhood is being reprogrammed by digital technologies that shape how young people learn, play, and connect. But children and young people are not experimental subjects, a captive market, or a commodity, which is why we must shape digital environments that protect and support their healthy development.
